title: The cross-package slide copy stops re-serializing and re-hashing packages it has already proven
decision: retained: 0587 item PPTX-2 implemented in full (physical-revision memo per immutable Snapshot, the candidate archive hashed while it is built, and the apply-time replan reusing the revisions the same call proved); two follow-ons named and left open
code_state: crates/litchi-pptx only: opened/model.rs (one private Snapshot field), opened/cross_copy_plan.rs, opened/cross_copy_plan/bounded_writer_tests.rs, opened/cross_copy_plan/revision_cache_tests.rs (new)
reason_codes: a cross-package slide copy serialized a complete package twelve times and hashed a complete graph twelve times per plan-plus-apply lifecycle; five of the serializations and four of the hashes reproduced a value the same call already held for the same bytes

a Snapshot owns its OpcPackage behind an Arc and never mutates it, so physical_package_fingerprint is a pure function of the snapshot and the archive bound it is taken under; the memo is keyed on that bound, lives only on the immutable capture, and is never inherited across Snapshot::rebound_to, where packages_equal proves graph equality but says nothing about the retained archive

build_candidate already writes the candidate archive into a bounded Vec that OpcPackage::from_vec_reusing_payloads reopens; digesting those bytes as they are written removes the second serialization without removing the bounded Vec that ADR 0005 requires

the four staleness proofs at the top of apply_plan and apply_patch are still taken from the live packages before any capture, so a stale or foreign source or destination is refused exactly where and how it was
no revision value and no proof format changed, so the durable LPCP0002 encoding is bit-identical and a patch serialized before this change still applies after it

accepted_evidence.call_counts: callgrind call counts per callee for package_fingerprint, physical_package_fingerprint, snapshot_physical_revision, bounded_package_bytes, capture_internal, prepare_cross_slide_copy_for_slides and PackageWriter::write_to_stream, both legs, two selectors, at --warmup 0 --samples 1 and 3
accepted_evidence.isolation_pair: callgrind at --samples 1 and --samples 3, differenced over two samples: per lifecycle the semantic hashes fall 12 -> 8, the archive serializations 9 -> 4, and write_to_stream 12 -> 7, on both selectors
accepted_evidence.symbol_accounting: the 8.76 G per-lifecycle fall on the media-rich corpus is accounted for exactly at this build's 52.07 Ir/byte software SHA-256 rate: 3.50 G of candidate hashing moved into bounded_package_bytes, 3.50 G of archive hashing and 5.26 G of graph hashing were removed
accepted_evidence.identity_cross_check: zlib_rs::deflate::deflate differs by 10,520 instructions in 5,955,591,941 per lifecycle (0.0002%), and the published output_sha256 is one value per corpus across all four timing legs
accepted_evidence.paired_timing: four legs in A1 B1 B2 A2 order, 30 measured samples after 3 warmups each, taskset -c 21, four selectors, with the A/A (A2 vs A1) and B/B (B2 vs B1) floors from the repeated legs in the same window, and the selectors' own plan/apply/publication/reopen phase clocks
accepted_evidence.native_cycles: perf stat whole child over the same four legs: cycles -8.39% against a -0.36% A/A floor, instructions -4.85%
accepted_evidence.correctness: cargo test -p litchi-pptx: 867 tests pass, seven new; cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy -p litchi-pptx --all-targets and cargo doc -p litchi-pptx --no-deps all clean

accepted_costs.instruction_counts: instructions rank work, not latency; callgrind runs SHA-256 in software because valgrind masks the SHA CPUID bit, so every hashing share here is about five times its native cycle share
accepted_costs.timing_floor: the wall-clock floors in this window are large -- the media-rich A/A floor is -4.99% at p50 and the plain lifecycle's B/B floor is -4.68% -- so pptx_cross_copy_plain (-4.84%) and pptx_cross_copy_plain_lifecycle (-1.26%) are inside their own noise and are reported rather than relied on
accepted_costs.corpora: both corpora are generated by litchi-pptx-cross-slide-copy-evidence-v1; the media-rich one is deliberately incompressible and its whole child is dominated by the harness's corpus construction and ten untimed refusal gates
accepted_costs.debug_assert: four debug_asserts re-derive every reused revision in debug and test builds, which roughly doubles the serializing and hashing the crate's own cross-copy tests perform
accepted_costs.host_load: other agents of the same wave were building and measuring on the other 31 cores throughout; the in-window A/A and B/B floors are the only statement about that

known_gaps.candidate_built_twice: the whole candidate is still built, serialized, deflated and captured twice per lifecycle -- once to plan, once to re-prove at apply; the copied closure's two deflations cost 5,955,591,941 Ir per media-rich lifecycle and are untouched. Retaining the planned candidate archive in CrossSlideCopyPlan would remove the second and changes the plan's memory profile under ADR 0005, so it needs a frozen design record
known_gaps.validate_candidate_capture: validate_candidate captures the candidate a second time after build_candidate captured it; its revision check is the proof that binds the candidate to the plan, so reusing that capture is a contract question rather than a value-identical reuse and is left open
known_gaps.remaining_hashes: four complete-package semantic hashes and four archive serializations remain per lifecycle; cutting the semantic ones needs 0587 item PPTX-1(c), which redefines the durable revision and needs a frozen design record and a magic bump for LPRM0001 and LPCP0002 (change 0590 recorded this)
known_gaps.provenance_question: 0587 asked whether build_candidate loses physical provenance. It does not: the candidate serialization uses soapberry_zip::preserve::PreservationIndex for the destination's own members and deflates only the nine copied parts (16,784,397 bytes, about 178 Ir per copied byte), because those are new members of the destination archive
known_gaps.external_fixture: the external-package copy binary was not run; its pinned LibreOffice QA fixture is not in the tree (change 0454 fetched it over the network and the artifact remains outside tracked source)
known_gaps.measurement: no allocation, RSS, cold-cache, range-source, concurrency or cross-platform measurement was taken, and no source-backed cross-copy selector exists to measure

withheld: any registered speedup, regression, RSS, allocation, cold-cache, real-producer or cross-platform result

provenance.host: AMD EPYC 9R45, 32 cores, 123 GiB, Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws, rustc 1.95.0, valgrind 3.26.0
